title: Matches, hands and drafts - House of Pips Wiki
description: How a House of Pips match runs from the hammer draw to the final hand: opening drafts, hand setup, Last Call, perk drafts, rerolls, Fresh Cut, saving a card, the Malus bargain and the hand summary.
html:
Matches, hands and drafts

A match is one game against Rival, from the first hammer draw until someone reaches the target score. It is made of hands (the table also says rounds; they are the same thing). Perks you draft last for the whole match and are gone when it ends.

How a match runs #

  1. Hammer draw. You and Rival each draw a face-down bone; the higher double takes the hammer and plays first.
  2. Opening drafts. You choose your opening perk, then Rival chooses theirs. In House of Malice both players also start with two random maluses.
  3. Each hand:
    1. Choose your bones for the hand (or take a random hand).
    2. The hand setup screen offers optional pre-hand actions.
    3. Play the hand. See Domino rules.
    4. Read the hand summary and receipts.
    5. If you won, keep or pass the hammer. Then the drafts for the next hand happen.
  4. Match end. The first player to reach the target while ahead wins. The final summary shows your match rewards.

Hand setup: optional actions before a hand #

Before the first bone lands you can use:

  • Last Call (free, once per match): mark one bone in your opening hand. If that bone is the last one you play when you go domino that hand, you win a jackpot of 750 XP and 750 Bone Bucks. If you play the marked bone earlier, Last Call expires.
  • Boneyard Lantern: light up one bone on your next boneyard trip.
  • Hammer Wax: improve the compensation draft if you win and pass the hammer.
  • Dealer's Dare: stake a supply on winning this hand.

Then choose Begin hand.

Drafts #

Perk drafts are where your build comes from.

Who drafts, and when #

  • At the start of the match you draft your opening perk, then Rival does.
  • After every hand, the loser drafts. In The Long Haul (and with the Double Down modifier) the loser drafts twice in a row.
  • If you win a hand and pass the hammer to Rival, you get a compensation draft before the loser's draft. Rival never passes the hammer.
  • Old School has no drafts at all.

What a draft offers #

A standard draft shows two perk cards and one Malus card. You take one card. Each Prestige rank adds one more perk card to your drafts (not in All In). Perk cards only come from perks you have unlocked in the Perks compendium; the Malus card can be any malus.

Why would you ever take the Malus? Usually you don't: you take a perk and the Malus goes away. Two buttons and a skill change that:

  • Take & Redraw (the Malus bargain): accept only the Malus, and the house deals you a fresh offer. Once per draft.
  • Take all, from the No Half Measures skill: take every card, perks and Malus together.

Some modes change the draft:

  • All In gives you every card automatically, Malus included.
  • Legendary Table shows three legendary perks and no Malus; choose one.

Changing the offer #

  • Reroll (Cut Again skill): replace one perk card with a fresh one. One free reroll per rank in every draft.
  • Save (Fortune Mortgage skill): reserve one perk card. It comes back as the first card of your next eligible draft, and you must take a different perk card now.
  • Fresh Cut (Fresh Cut perk): upgrade the lowest-rarity perk card by one rarity.
  • Perk Echo (skill): a perk you take may echo as a temporary extra copy for the next hand.

Draft odds #

Common perks show up most often and legendary perks least. Several things raise your odds of rarer cards: the Fortune skills Loaded Luck, Gilded Draw, Golden Thread and Lucky Recovery, and Hammer Wax on a compensation draft. In single-player, legendary perks only appear once you have unlocked them. Online, every legendary perk the match allows can appear for both players.

The hammer choice #

When you win a hand (and the match isn't over), you choose:

  • Keep the hammer: you lead the next hand. Only Rival drafts.
  • Pass the hammer: Rival leads the next hand, and you get a compensation draft before Rival's loser draft.

Leading is an advantage: the hammer holder sets the first open ends and plays one bone ahead.

The hand summary and receipts #

After each hand the summary shows the score change and the hand award. Two receipt pages follow:

  • The XP receipt lists where your XP came from. See Career, XP and Bone Bucks.
  • The Bone Bucks receipt lists every Bone Buck you earned.

The ledger #

Open the Ledger at any time during a match (or press L). It lists every play with its open-end total, each perk bonus and malus, every perk and supply you or Rival used, and boneyard trips. If a score surprises you, the ledger shows exactly where it came from.

Leaving a match #

Your match is saved automatically. Save and exit in Settings returns you to the menu, and CONTINUE on the main menu brings you back. See Saving, Continue and Steam Cloud for Rage quit.
